A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RATE study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be reliably matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original semi-synthetic experiments, reward-model evaluations, and rewrite analyses in Section 5 and appendices C–E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including treatment-effect estimates, correlation-shift experiments, and scored rewrite examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same double-rewrite procedure and ATT, ATU, and ATE estimators. Added explanatory passages introduce no procedural component.

E1.justification: Both versions use IMDB, ELI5, HelpSteer, and HH-RLHF with the same attribute interventions and correlation-shift scenarios. Appendix coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The semi-synthetic comparisons retain the naive and single-rewrite estimators. Figure 5 retains RATE versus naive estimation for the same three reward models; appendix comparator membership is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same sampling procedures, stated sample sizes, context-length filtering, and evaluation metrics. The new discussion of diagnosing cancellation failures does not report a new or revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The typo and correlation-shift tests, single-versus-double rewrite analyses, and qualitative failure examples are retained in Section 5 and appendices C–E. v3 adds interpretation of existing tests, not additional analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same 95% confidence-interval practice and normal-approximation rationale in Appendix A. No repeated-run, seed, or statistical-estimation reporting changes were found.

E6.justification: The empirical plots in Figures 2–10 and numerical reward examples in Table 2 and Appendix E are unchanged. No result entries, numerical findings, or reported trends are added or removed.

T1.justification: The treatment-effect definitions, assumptions, Theorem 4.1, and Appendix B proof are unchanged. Numbering the rewrite-error equation and adding commentary about the theorem's scope do not revise its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same causal-explanation objective, double-rewrite contribution, conditional validity guarantee, and empirical-effectiveness claims.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly emphasizes that the theorem supplies sufficient conditions demonstrating that RATE can be consistent. Section 5 adds that sensitivity to target/off-target correlations can indicate failed error cancellation, giving an explicit diagnostic interpretation to existing experiments.

D1.justification: The GPT-4o-2024-08-06 rewriter, BatchAPI usage, costs, rewrite instructions, and code/model/data access disclosures are retained in Section 5 and appendices A and E.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Wachter et al. (2018) and explicitly distinguishes RATE's average attribute effects from minimal-perturbation counterfactual explanations, also referencing the already-cited Jiang et al. (2024). Section 6 otherwise retains its positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording and punctuation edits, moves a literature paragraph within the introduction, and adds short clarifications. Author and publication text are updated; the overall section organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces the helpfulness/length-confounding diagram with a three-column overview of naive, single-rewrite, and RATE estimation. Its caption is rewritten, Table 1's caption is edited, and several figures shift position with text reflow.

improvement.justification: Relative to v2, v3 better distinguishes the research objective from counterfactual explanations and explicitly explains the limited role of Theorem 4.1 and the diagnostic interpretation of existing experiments. The redesigned Figure 1 supports this exposition. These are useful clarity improvements, while the method, mathematical guarantees, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
